text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high request latency & elevated 5xx rate on inference-prod-west-1 (p95 latency > 1200ms, 5xx spike)
alex_oncall: paging in — looking now, is this tied to a specific model or region?
lee_sre: seeing sustained queue growth on batcher-gpu-pool-3, backlog ~4200 reqs, continuous-batcher depth climbing
jamie_oncall: confirmed, model-redwood-xl-v2 showing heavy long-sequence traffic from a handful of customers, tail tokens blowing up KV cache churn
alex_oncall: initial mitigation plan: 1) reduce per-tenant concurrent requests (soft cap) 2) bump batch window to favor throughput and shed latency-sensitive small requests 3) throttle low-priority routes 4) disable streaming/chunked responses if cheap to do.
maya_cs: heads-up — customer @AcmeCorp reported timeouts, their requests are long context summarizations, impacted most.
alex_oncall: executing quick changes now. will document commands.
eng-runtime-bot: Applying config: 
```
# temporary quickpatch
routes.acmeCorp.rate_limit.per_minute = 1200 -> 300
runtime.batch.continuous.max_latency_ms = 40 -> 180
runtime.batch.continuous.max_batch_tokens = 8192 -> 16384
features.streaming_chunked_responses.enabled = true -> false
```
lee_sre: runbook note: increasing max_latency_ms increases batching -> higher throughput, expect p95 latency to rise but system-level 5xxs should drop as queue eviction reduces.
jamie_oncall: also planting a dynamic rate-shaper to prioritize small interactive routes: lowpri service class will be capped at 20% of burst capacity.
alex_oncall: applied per-tenant soft caps for top 6 noisy tenants. commands: 
```
redwoodctl tenancy cap set --tenant acmecorp --concurrency 8 --reason "live mitigation"
redwoodctl runtime config set continuous.max_latency_ms=180 --env prod-west-1
redwoodctl feature toggle streaming_chunked_responses off --env prod-west-1
```
eng-runtime-bot: change applied; GC pause and warmup for larger batches expected, monitoring.
maya_cs: AcmeCorp acknowledged; asked for ETA.
lee_sre: telemetry after change (10m): inbound qps down ~12% overall, 5xx rate down 78%, queue depth reduced from 4200 -> 700, p95 latency increased from ~420ms -> ~890ms for long requests, small interactive routes saw some tail increases too.
jamie_oncall: trade-off noted: higher p95 but far fewer 5xx and much better throughput. this is acceptable for now.
alex_oncall: next step: enable traffic-shaper that redistributes spare capacity to critical tenants, and create temporary quota bump for enterprise customers that pay for reserved capacity.
eng-runtime-bot: Applied traffic-shaper: lowpri.weight=0.2, highpri.weight=0.8
lee_sre: also evicted stuck KV caches on two nodes: `ssh gpu-node-45 sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime` — cleared hot cache churn, small transient token regen.
alex_oncall: notifying oncall-night (handoff) — jamie, I'll hand this at 21:00 UTC. mitigation checklist: 1) per-tenant caps in place 2) batch window increased to 180ms 3) streaming disabled 4) traffic-shaper weights updated 5) nodes restarted where necessary 6) CS notified.
jamie_oncall: taking the handoff, will monitor for 2h and prepare rollback plan if customer impact unacceptable. please leave any evidence logs.
alex_oncall: logs: `/var/log/redwood/prod-west1/batcher/3301122334.log` — included trace ids for AcmeCorp requests.
maya_cs: I'll keep AcmeCorp updated: they prefer higher latency over errors; will confirm acceptance.
lee_sre: checklist for follow-up: - measure token-level cost delta - check KV cache hitrate after warmup - consider targeted model-quantization for heavy tenants if recurring - schedule a postmortem if incident >1h impact
jamie_oncall: ack. if p95 for small interactive routes stays >600ms after 30m, I'll reduce max_latency_ms to 120 and tighten lowpri caps further.
alex_oncall: thanks team. :white_check_mark: handing over.
incident-bot: Handoff recorded: from alex_oncall to jamie_oncall at 2026-03-17T21:00:00Z. thread closed for primary pager.
